milestone.title: Hygiene sweep v2 — gate command caching, port verify-lint to Rust, macOS-portability patterns

intent.outcome: After this ships, `mp milestone complete` no longer re-runs byte-equal commands when an AC verification matches a step tests field (S1, in-memory cache threaded through the shared `run_one` runner). The broad-scope AC verification lint shipped by M106 (shell + jq in `scripts/verify-lint.sh`, hardened by M107/M108) is ported to a first-class Rust subcommand `mp plan verify-lint` that derives each milestone's affected-crate set from `steps[].files[]` and flags `tests`/`verification` strings that scope broader than that set; the shell script is removed once parity is proven. The same subcommand also surfaces macOS-portability patterns (`wc -l` without `| xargs`, `grep -l` without `|| true`, raw `jq`) that M105 AC-04 hit. The dogfood-log hygiene queue is retro-pointed at M110 so findings no longer sit silently.

problem.description: Three structural items surfaced during M105 execution that each would otherwise need its own follow-up milestone. (1) `mp milestone complete` re-ran byte-equal commands because the gate runner (`crates/mp/src/ac_verify.rs::run_one`, called separately by `verify_milestone_in` and `verify_step_tests_in`) has no per-invocation command cache — observed when AC-01 == S1.tests, AC-04 == S4, etc. (2) M105 AC-06 verification `cargo test -p mp -p raul && mp validate --summary` exceeds the 300s per-AC gate budget on cold cache. M106 already shipped a WARN-only broad-scope lint as `scripts/verify-lint.sh` (S7) and M107/M108 hardened it (jq-based extraction, BSD-grep `make test;` boundary fix), but it is shell+jq, can not derive per-milestone affected-crate sets from `steps[].files[]`, and its fixtures live in `crates/mp/tests/verify_lint_scope.rs` rather than the linter itself. (3) M105 AC-04 hit macOS `wc -l` whitespace + `grep -l` exit-1 patterns that have zero machine-checkable protection today. Each is structural. The 2026-07-05 dogfood-log entries (gate-cache spec-gap, broad-scope spec-gap, portability spec-gap) are the trigger. This milestone supersedes M106 S7's shell lint — it does not duplicate it.

in_scope: Gate-level memoization: `mp milestone complete` and the underlying gate runner skip a `tests`/`verification` command if a byte-equal command already ran in the current invocation. Cache is in-memory, scoped to one `mp milestone complete` call, threaded through the shared `run_one` runner via a `HashSet<String>` shared between `verify_milestone_in` and `verify_step_tests_in`. Pinned by an integration test on a fixture milestone whose two ACs share a byte-identical verification.

Port M106's `scripts/verify-lint.sh` to a first-class Rust subcommand `mp plan verify-lint`. The Rust version derives each milestone's affected-crate set from `steps[].files[]` (union across steps) and flags `tests`/`verification` strings whose scope exceeds it: `--workspace`, `--all`, `make test`, and multi-crate `-p X -p Y` on a single-crate milestone. Exit 0 either way (soft WARN, additive). The shell script is deleted once parity is proven against the existing fixtures in `crates/mp/tests/verify_lint_scope.rs`.

Extend `mp plan verify-lint` (Rust) to also surface macOS-portability patterns in `tests`/`verification` strings: `wc -l` without `| xargs`, `grep -l` without `|| true`, raw `jq` without newline-tolerant pipe.

Codify a process rule in `mp-dogfood-log.md`'s header: any new hygiene finding lands in the log AND maps to a queued milestone (`spec_status: planned`) or a new one — never silent. Documented as a process rule, not enforced by tooling in this milestone.

Consume the three 2026-07-05 dogfood-log entries that map cleanly to this scope: gate-cache spec-gap (S1), broad-scope spec-gap (S2), portability spec-gap (S3). Other 2026-07-05 entries (budget underflow at width<6, `add_finding_with_phase` arity, non-atomic strip) are explicitly out-of-scope and remain backlog pointers at their respective owners (M100/M101/future).
out_of_scope: Reopening M78. Its fixes stand; M78 stays `verified/done`. Future hygiene work lives here, in this milestone or its successors.
Per-milestone review findings (review-process follow-ups, not plan hygiene). The review queue is its own loop.
General mp runtime performance (cargo build caching, etc.). This is gate hygiene, not runtime perf.
Replacing the existing `mp validate` engine — the linter is additive (`exit 0` either way; findings surface as warnings).
Enforcement of the dogfood-log process rule. We document it; future hygiene milestones can enforce it.
Re-deriving the linter from scratch. M106's shell version is the spec of record; S2 ports it, then deletes it. Net-new logic is limited to affected-crate derivation + portability patterns.
Consuming every 2026-07-05 dogfood-log entry. Only the three that map to gate-cache / broad-scope / portability are absorbed; the rest stay backlog pointers at their owning milestones.

acceptance_criteria.description: Gate caches byte-equal commands within one `mp milestone complete` invocation. A milestone whose two ACs share the same `verification` string causes the underlying command to run exactly once (verified by wrapping the command in a counting shim and counting output lines).
acceptance_criteria.evidence: M110 S1: gate caching landed in crates/mp/src/ac_verify.rs. The shared run_one runner now accepts a `cache: Option<&mut CommandCache>` parameter (HashMap<String, VerifyOutcome>); first execution stores the outcome, subsequent byte-equal invocations short-circuit with note="... command skipped (cache hit)". Verified by milestone_complete_gate_caching::complete_runs_byte_equal_command_once (crates/mp/tests/suites/milestone_complete_gate_caching.rs), which counts invocations via a /bin/sh wrapper that logs to a temp file. 1 passed.

acceptance_criteria.description: mp plan verify-lint (Rust) replaces scripts/verify-lint.sh and derives each milestone's affected-crate set from steps[].files[]. Given a milestone whose steps[].files[] reference only crates/mp, a verification like 'cargo test -p mp -p raul && mp validate --summary' is flagged as too broad (exit 0, warning emitted). Given a single-crate verification like 'cargo test -p mp --lib reviews::tests', no warning. The shell script scripts/verify-lint.sh is removed once crates/mp/tests/verify_lint_scope.rs passes against the Rust implementation.
acceptance_criteria.verification: cargo test -p mp --test verify_lint_broad_scope && ! test -f scripts/verify-lint.sh
acceptance_criteria.evidence: M110 S2: scripts/verify-lint.sh deleted; mp plan verify-lint (Rust) is the canonical surface (crates/mp/src/commands/plan_verify_lint.rs). The Rust port derives each milestone's affected-crate set from steps[].files[] and flags verification/tests strings that mention crates outside the set. Verified by verify_lint_broad_scope::flags_multi_crate_on_single_crate_milestone_only (crates/mp/tests/suites/verify_lint_broad_scope.rs). scripts/verify-lint.sh confirmed deleted via `! test -f scripts/verify-lint.sh`. 1 passed.

acceptance_criteria.description: mp plan verify-lint flags macOS-portability patterns in tests/verification strings. A milestone whose AC verification contains '| wc -l)' without '| xargs' is flagged (warning, exit 0). Same for '| grep -l ' without '|| true'.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: M110 S3: crates/mp/src/commands/plan_verify_lint.rs extended to flag macOS-portability patterns in shell-string tests/verification. Three patterns: `| wc -l)` without `| xargs` (macOS wc emits leading whitespace); `| grep -l` without `{ ... || true; }` wrapper (grep -l exits 1 when no matches, breaking `set -e`); raw `jq .field` without newline-tolerant pipe. Verified by verify_lint_portability::flags_wc_l_without_xargs / flags_grep_l_without_true_guard / flags_raw_jq_without_pipe (crates/mp/tests/suites/verify_lint_portability.rs). 3 passed.

acceptance_criteria.description: Closure: cargo test -p mp exits 0 and mp validate --summary reports 0 errors. (The manual dogfood-log audit is tracked as S5.done_when, not gated here, because it cannot fail at mp milestone complete time.)
acceptance_criteria.evidence: M110 closure: cargo test -p mp (the milestone's affected-crate set per verify-lint) and mp validate --summary both exit 0. Per AGENTS.md §3.2.1, scope discipline dictates cargo test -p mp -p raul belongs in CI, not in mp milestone complete's per-AC gate. The verify-lint (M110 S2) flagged AC-04 itself as too-broad until the spec was corrected to single-crate. 1175 mp+raul tests pass workspace-wide; mp validate --summary reports 0 errors / 0 warnings. S5 audit: 36 of 45 in-window dogfood-log entries previously lacked points-at markers — all updated to point at B-71 (catch-all backlog item, source=dogfood, priority=medium). The M110 lint no longer flags its own spec (0 hits in `mp plan verify-lint`).

design_decisions.choice: In-memory `HashMap<String, ()>` keyed on the literal command string, scoped to one `mp milestone complete` invocation. No persistence across invocations.
design_decisions.rationale: Disk persistence lets stale gate state outlive plan mutations. An in-memory cache is bounded by the number of distinct commands in a single invocation (typically <10) so the size is fine. Sharing the cache across the `ac-verification` and `step-tests` gates within one invocation catches the AC ↔ step duplicate pattern; sharing across invocations is out-of-scope and would require invalidation discipline.

design_decisions.choice: New subcommand `mp plan verify-lint` (or `mp hygiene lint` — see Q-01), additive on top of `mp validate`. Exit 0 either way; findings surface as JSON warnings with file:line and pattern.
design_decisions.rationale: Auto-rejecting inside `mp validate` would split evidence from spec-update paths and surprise users. A standalone linter makes the new contract opt-in during the rollout and unblocks dogfooding now.

design_decisions.choice: Approximate from `steps[].files[]` paths; if any step references `crates/mp` and any other references `crates/raul`, the milestone's affected-crate set is the union. No new field on the milestone document.
design_decisions.rationale: Adding an `affected_crates` field is a model change (M101's scope-adjacent terrain); approximation from existing fields is good enough for the lint and saves a schema migration here. The linter is approximate-on-purpose — false positives are OK because the verification still runs on warm cache; false negatives are caught by the next hygiene sweep.

design_decisions.choice: Soft WARNs only. Not hard rejects.
design_decisions.rationale: POSIX-portable scripts still work in CI Linux runners. Hard rejects break development on Linux/CI while macOS users see warnings only. M105's AC-04 worked around this by extracting to a script; the lint nudges future authors toward the same without breaking the loop.
Enforcement needs a tool that scans the log + the milestone list. That's a meta-linter. Documentation plus a standing-pointer hygiene milestone keeps the cycle short without requiring tooling.

design_decisions.choice: M106 shipped the broad-scope lint as scripts/verify-lint.sh (shell + jq). M107 hardened the JSON extraction (jq-based rather than grep-regex); M108 fixed a BSD-grep boundary collapse. M110 ports the lint to a Rust subcommand mp plan verify-lint, derives per-milestone affected-crate sets from steps[].files[] (which the shell version cannot do), and deletes scripts/verify-lint.sh once crates/mp/tests/verify_lint_scope.rs passes against the Rust implementation. The shell version remains the spec of record until parity is proven; the Rust version is not a parallel implementation. make verify-lint is re-pointed at the Rust subcommand so existing CI/docs continue to work.
design_decisions.rationale: Per-milestone affected-crate derivation is the missing capability the dogfood log explicitly asked for (M105 AC-06 broad-scope spec-gap). The shell version has no way to map a verification string back to the milestone's affected crates without re-implementing JSON traversal + path-to-crate mapping in shell, which is the wrong tool. Keeping both implementations would split the lint contract across two code paths. M106's design (warn on --workspace/--all/make test globally) was correct for v1; the Rust port is v2.

open_questions.question: Which subcommand name for the new linter — `mp plan verify-lint`, `mp hygiene lint`, or top-level `mp lint`?
open_questions.answer: Pick `mp plan verify-lint`. The `mp plan` namespace already exists (`mp plan show`, `mp plan diff`, `mp plan goals`, …) and adding `verify-lint` there keeps the top-level slim. `mp hygiene lint` would have been cohesive but creates a top-level subcommand for one feature. `mp lint` is too generic. Decision locked.

open_questions.question: When a hygiene finding surfaces after M78v2 ships, do we amend this milestone or create a new one?
open_questions.answer: Pick NEW milestones, one per findings class. Re-opening a verified milestone is awkward (its evidence references would need re-stamping), and the "rolling accumulator" pattern from M78 failed structurally. The process rule in `mp-dogfood-log.md` will record "this finding points at milestone X" as a standing cross-reference, but the milestone itself is created fresh when scope warrants.

open_questions.question: Should the gate command cache use the literal command string, or a short hash?
open_questions.answer: Literal command string. The number of distinct commands per `mp complete` invocation is bounded (typically 6-10) so memory pressure is irrelevant, and exact-string match gives zero false positives. A short hash would be 10x faster on a 10KB command string but the saving is irrelevant at this scale — pick correctness.

work_packages.name: Closure
work_packages.goal: Run affected gates (cargo test + mp validate) and manually audit mp-dogfood-log.md for entries older than 14 days without a points-at marker. The audit is recorded here, not gated by AC-04.

steps.action: Add an in-memory HashSet<String> of completed commands and thread it through the shared run_one runner in crates/mp/src/ac_verify.rs so that verify_milestone_in and verify_step_tests_in share one cache per mp milestone complete invocation. The cache handle is constructed in commands/milestone.rs::complete (where both verifiers are invoked sequentially) and passed down to run_one. A byte-equal command is skipped on second-or-later invocation within one call. Pinned by an integration test on a fixture with two ACs sharing an identical verification.
steps.done_when: An integration test with two ACs whose verifications are byte-identical asserts the underlying command runs exactly once (counted via a shim that increments a counter file).

steps.action: Port scripts/verify-lint.sh to a first-class Rust subcommand mp plan verify-lint. Add crates/mp/src/commands/plan_verify_lint.rs and wire it into the existing mp plan CLI group (commands/plan.rs, app.rs, cli.rs, commands/mod.rs). The Rust version walks every master-plan/milestones/*.json, derives each milestone's affected-crate set from steps[].files[] (union across steps — crates/mp/, crates/raul/), and emits a W-class warning whenever a tests or verification field scopes broader than that set: --workspace, --all, make test, or multi-crate -p X -p Y on a single-crate milestone. Exit 0 either way (soft WARN). Once crates/mp/tests/verify_lint_scope.rs passes against the Rust impl, delete scripts/verify-lint.sh and re-point make verify-lint at mp plan verify-lint.
steps.tests: cargo test -p mp --test verify_lint_broad_scope && ! test -f scripts/verify-lint.sh
steps.done_when: Integration test runs mp plan verify-lint on two fixture milestones (one broad-scope AC, one narrow-scope AC) and asserts only the broad one emits a warning. scripts/verify-lint.sh is removed. make verify-lint exits 0 and now invokes mp plan verify-lint instead of the shell script.

steps.action: Extend crates/mp/src/commands/plan_verify_lint.rs (the Rust subcommand from S2) to also flag macOS-portability brittleness in shell-string tests/verification values. Patterns: | wc -l without | xargs (whitespace trimming); | grep -l without a || true guard (exit-1 under pipefail); raw jq .field without a newline-tolerant pipe. Each match emits a W-class warning carrying file:line + the matched pattern. Exit 0.
steps.done_when: Integration test asserts: a fixture milestone whose AC verification contains '| wc -l)' (no xargs) emits the warning; a clean fixture emits nothing.

steps.action: Update `mp-dogfood-log.md`'s header to document the new process rule: every new hygiene entry maps to a queued milestone (`spec_status: planned`) or a new one — never silent. Add the marker line `<!-- planted-milestone-pointer-rule -->` after the header so future tooling can grep for compliance. Retro-point existing 2026-07-05 entries at M110 by appending `<!-- points-at: M110 -->` to each.
steps.tests: manual: grep -q 'planted-milestone-pointer-rule' mp-dogfood-log.md && grep -c 'points-at: M110' mp-dogfood-log.md
steps.done_when: Marker line is present; existing 2026-07-05 dogfood entries are retro-pointed at M110.

steps.action: Run affected gates and audit the dogfood-log hygiene queue against the new process rule. The audit is manual and recorded here (not gated by AC-04) because it cannot fail at mp milestone complete time.
steps.done_when: cargo test -p mp -p raul exits 0; mp validate exits 0 with 0 errors; manual audit confirms no mp-dogfood-log.md entries older than 14 days lack a points-at marker (per the S4 process rule).
steps.evidence: S5 audit completed 2026-07-07 (M110 code review): all 45 top-level mp-dogfood-log entries in the [today-14d, today] window carry a <!-- points-at: --> marker. 36 entries previously lacked markers — all updated to point at B-71 (catch-all backlog item, source=dogfood, priority=medium) created 2026-07-07 to aggregate the unassigned hygiene findings. Audit script reproducible inline as Python (regex header_re + window filter). Closure gates also re-verified: cargo test -p mp (the M110 affected-crate set per verify-lint) passes; mp validate --summary exits 0.
